newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria says resumes operations in Nembe.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria says resumes operations in Nembe.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Friday it has resumed operations at one of five oil stations in Nembe creek, in the southeast, shut down since last Saturday because of a political dispute between villagers and the military government.
"We resumed operations at Nembe 1 at 1530 gmt today after reaching an agreement with the communities involved in the dispute," a spokesman told Reuters in Lagos.
Villagers protesting against a merger of two communities into one local government area in the recently created Bayelsa state ordered Shell to stop oil production in the oil stations.
Nembe 1 has a production output of 42,000 barrels per day of the total output of 110,000 bpd total output for the five stations shut in there since Saturday, the Shell spokesman said.
He said the company could not resume production in the other four stations because of time factor, adding, "By tomorrow we will swing into production action in the other stations."
The spokesman maintained the five flow stations involved in that sector had not been occupied by the villagers.
Villagers in the communities only told the company to shut down and evacuate the flow stations within 12 hours, he said, adding that a small police contigent had been guarding the facilities.
The communities are Ogbolomobiri and Bassambiri, which the government fused to produce one local government council chairman in municipal polls on March 15.
Earlier, Shell said it would send a team to assess six flow stations in its western division occupied for days by Ijaw tribesmen involved in another political protest.

The occupation of the stations near midwestern Warri town, which forced Shell cut back production output of 100,000 bpd, ended on Thursday when the protesters freed the last batch of 127 Nigerian Shell workers they were holding hostage.

The oil communities have long been restive over the lack of modern amenities in their areas despite being the place where Nigeria derives the money that sustains the country and they frequently vent their wrath on oil companies.
